subject: research/stop-twin
professional: a senior statistician in sequential analysis and rare-event simulation (the kind who reviews for The American Statistician, Sequential Analysis or ACM TOMACS). They would check first that the inverse-sampling estimator, its variance law and the exact interval are right (Haldane 1945, Best 1974, Mikulski & Smith 1976, Clopper-Pearson-type inversion), whether the 'sequential Wald' straw man is the rule the cited Chow & Robbins (1965) paper actually proposes, and whether the nearest prior work on relative-precision stopping (Dagum, Karp, Luby & Ross 2000; Frey 2010) is cited

evidence.correctness: Every headline number reproduces and recomputes independently. Rerun: `cd research/stop-twin && PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` (97 s) is byte-identical to experiments/results.txt (diff empty). Independent script %s/indep.py and indep2.py (scipy 1.18 / numpy 2.5, imports nothing from the package except exact_ci for side-by-side comparison): (1) negative-binomial moments from scipy.stats.nbinom give E[(m-1)/(N-1)]/p = 1.000000 for all six (m,p), E[m/N]/p 1.2301/1.2496/1.0326/1.0344/1.0096/1.0101 and sd/p 0.5500/0.5768/0.1839/0.1889/0.0984/0.1010, equal to section 0 to 4 dp; all sit below the Mikulski-Smith (1976) bound sqrt((1-p)/(m-2)) (0.5627 at m=5,p=0.05). (2) exact_ci equals the beta-quantile closed form lo=I^-1(a/2; m, n-m+1), hi=I^-1(1-a/2; m, n-m) to 1e-11 at (30,30000),(10,10000),(100,95000),(3,50). (3) exact coverage of that interval by summing the nbinom pmf at p=1e-3 is 0.95002/0.95001/0.95001/0.95001 at m=10/30/100/400, and E[hi/lo] 3.561/2.057/1.481/1.217, matching the paper's Monte Carlo 95.0-95.5%% and 3.56/2.06/1.48/1.22 exactly on the ratio. (4) An exact Markov-chain computation of the sequential Wald rule on the n0=step=100 grid (binomial convolution, no simulation) gives P(stop with 0 failures) 0.3660/0.9048/0.9900, coverage 0.600/0.090/0.009 and mean p^/p 0.631/0.095 at p=1e-2/1e-3/1e-4 (paper MC: 0.372/0.901/0.991, 0.597/0.096/0.009, 0.627/0.098), and coverage 0.941 with a >=1-failure guard (paper 0.938): all within 1 Monte Carlo SE. (5) Planning table: n=z^2(1-p0)/(0.04 p0)=95940.4, delivered relative half-widths 0.063/0.200/0.365/0.633/2.001 and P(0 failures at 1e-5)=0.3831 recomputed. Not 4: the 1/sqrt(m-2) law drops the (1-p) factor of the known bound, which is the whole of the '6%% at m=5, p=0.05' gap the paper calls asymptotic; the paper's 95.5%% upper coverage is Monte Carlo noise (exact is 95.00%%).

evidence.verification: `cd research/stop-twin && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 8 tests OK in 0.99 s. Good tests where they exist (pmf sums to 1, Haldane exact unbiasedness, variance law, binomial identity, the zero-failure trap). Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, 1 caught, 4 survived: exact_ci upper limit using Bin(n,p) instead of Bin(n-1,p) (model.py:82) and the lower limit at alpha instead of alpha/2 (model.py:81) both survive because the only interval test is a loose bracket plus coverage >= 0.92 on 400 draws; inverse_sample losing the +1 per geometric gap (model.py:110, N biased low by m) survives; wald_half dropping (1-ph) (model.py:88) survives (near-equivalent at small p, so weakest evidence). The min_fail comparison >= -> > (model.py:100) is caught. No test pins exact_ci against the beta-quantile closed form or checks inverse_sample's mean m/p.
evidence.craft: Read src/stop_twin/model.py (121 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py. Stdlib only, small pure functions with formula docstrings, log-space pmf, exact moments by pmf summation, O(m) geometric-gap sampler, figure parsed from results.txt. Defects: no input validation (p outside (0,1), m<2 gives haldane division by zero at n=1, exact_ci bisect bracket hard-coded to [1e-12, 0.999] so p above 0.999 or below 1e-12 silently clamps), `from stop_twin import *` in tests and run.py, sequential_wald returns silently at nmax=1e7 without a flag, run.py is a single 97 s loop with no option for fewer reps.
evidence.claims: Checked: every number in README line 3 and whitepaper Results 1-5 is in results.txt and recomputes (above). 'exact (1-p)^100 = 90.5%%' holds (0.9048). Limits and 'Stylised' disclosure are explicit and accurate. Problems, none changing a number: README line 10 says '~1 min', measured 97 s; README line 3 and whitepaper:14 say the >=1-failure guard 'restores' Wald coverage at 0.938, which is 1.2 points under nominal (exact 0.941); README:13 'Builds on' names two CU Boulder groups whose work is not used, and the Zhao et al. 2020 sim-to-real survey (whitepaper:28) is listed but never cited in the text; Chow & Robbins (1965) is cited as the classical fixed-width rule, but the paper does not say that rule's +1/n term already prevents the zero-failure stop. [Lead session review: lowered from 3 to 2. Two of this audit's own claim checks are partial, and the README cites Chow & Robbins (1965) as the classical method while showing a plug-in rule fail that Chow & Robbins' +1/n term avoids, without saying so; a reader takes away a wrong conclusion about the classical method. The bar verdict is unchanged (verification 2).]
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher choosing a stopping rule for a rare-failure twin run. The note gives a correct, runnable recipe (inverse sampling, (m-1)/(N-1), exact beta-quantile interval, m=2+1/r^2) and a vivid failure case, which is useful as a teaching note. As research it does not hold novelty: inverse sampling and its unbiased estimator (Haldane 1945), its exact variance (Best 1974) and the bound p^2(1-p)/(m-2) (Mikulski & Smith 1976), and relative-precision stopping by running to a fixed number of successes (Dagum, Karp, Luby & Ross 2000, SIAM J. Comput., the Stopping Rule Algorithm) are all known; only Haldane is cited. The zero-variance trap of naive sequential Wald is exactly what the 1/n term in Chow & Robbins (1965) and the fixed-width sequential proportion literature (Frey 2010, Am. Stat. 64:242) address. My exact chain shows the Chow-Robbins rule with that term at p=1e-3, eps=2e-4 stops with zero failures in 5.5e-5 of runs and covers 0.942, i.e. the cited classical rule is already safe and the paper's 'sequential Wald' is a straw man. The case a practitioner actually has (a cap on run length, censoring) is left to Next steps. Not in any programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md.
evidence.domain: Against standard sequential-analysis practice: the inverse-sampling estimator and its exact interval are textbook-correct and the computations are exact, which a statistician would sign off. They would not sign off the framing: the compared rule omits the Chow-Robbins correction the paper itself cites, the variance law is presented as the author's asymptotic approximation without the (1-p) factor or the known bound, the guard result is one configuration, and the operational design (capped run with censoring, or a DKLR-style (eps,delta) guarantee) is not analysed.

defects.what: The compared 'sequential Wald' rule is a straw man: Chow & Robbins (1965), which the README cites as the classical method, stops when n >= (z/eps)^2 (v_n + 1/n); the +1/n term prevents the zero-failure stop (exact chain: P(stop with 0)=5.5e-5, coverage 0.942 at p=1e-3). The paper never says so, so a reader concludes classical fixed-width sequential stopping fails

Nearest prior work uncited and novelty implicit: exact variance (Best 1974) and bound p^2(1-p)/(m-2) (Mikulski & Smith 1976) of the Haldane estimator, run-to-k-successes relative (eps,delta) stopping (Dagum, Karp, Luby & Ross 2000), fixed-width sequential proportion intervals (Frey 2010). The 1/sqrt(m-2) law is presented as the author's asymptotic, minus the (1-p) factor

exact_ci and inverse_sample are untested at the value level: 3 of 4 non-equivalent mutants in them survive (upper limit n vs n-1, lower limit alpha vs alpha/2, geometric gap off by one); the only interval test is a bracket plus coverage >= 0.92

No input validation: m<2 divides by zero in haldane, exact_ci bisect bracket fixed at [1e-12, 0.999] silently clamps, sequential_wald returns at nmax without a flag

verdict: A small, correct teaching note. Every number I recomputed (scipy negative-binomial moments, beta-quantile closed form for the exact interval, exact coverage 0.95001 by pmf summation, an exact Markov-chain version of the sequential Wald trap, the planning table) matches results.txt within Monte Carlo error, and the experiment reproduces byte-for-byte. It misses the bar on verification: 4 of 5 seeded mutants survive, including both limits of exact_ci. As research it is below the repository's PhD bar: the content is classical (Haldane 1945, Best 1974, Mikulski & Smith 1976, Dagum et al. 2000), most of that prior work is uncited, and the 'sequential Wald' it shows failing omits the +1/n term of the Chow-Robbins rule the README cites, which by exact computation removes the trap.
